gaps.note: Cut hides the immediate reaction of the panel to the end of the prepared presentation.
Cut hides the immediate transition after Mark's exit.

stage_a.note: They maintain high energy, smile constantly, and dance during the demonstration.
Very strong excitement shown through their upbeat delivery and eager product demonstration.
They are friendly and approachable, smiling warmly as they introduce themselves.

venture.description: Electric self-balancing individual skates that users can ride and maneuver independently.
venture.note: The founders seek capital to innovate on existing catalog designs.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 expresses a brief reaction of interest before the pitch begins.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 states that the product looks cool as the founders enter.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 introduces himself to the panel.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 introduces himself to the panel.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states their location, company name, and asks for one hundred twenty-five thousand dollars for twenty percent equity.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 describes the rising trend of electric rideables and consumer fascination with them.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 introduces Zuum shoes as self-balancing platforms with an eight mile per hour top speed and one hour ride time.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 suggests they demonstrate to the panel how the shoes work.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 agrees to see the demonstration.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 explains the different ways to ride and maneuver the shoes, including practicing dance moves.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 demonstrates riding and dancing on the shoes.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 jokes that the dancing looks just like S4.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 jokingly mocks their presentation style by imitating them.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states their dedication to making electric rideables accessible to the masses.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 asks which investor wants to join them in the future.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 expresses a desire to try the product.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 jokingly reminds S2 of his children before he tries it.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 asks S3 if he wants to try riding the shoes.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 declines the offer to try the shoes.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 gives S2 instructions on how to lean forward and backward to move.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks if users feel like they are going to fall off.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 encourages S1 to try the shoes.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 jokingly says goodbye to S2 as he rides.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 jokingly suggests locking the doors so S2 cannot leave.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks if S2 could stop himself or not after he gets off.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 comments that getting on is easy but getting off is difficult.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 agrees that stopping is harder and requires practice to master.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks how the shoes handle city obstacles like potholes and divots in the street.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 clarifies they do not see the shoes as an alternative to walking in the city.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 adds that the shoes are convenient because they can be thrown into a backpack.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks for the retail price of the shoes.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states the retail price is two hundred ninety-nine dollars.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks what the landed cost of the shoes is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states the landed cost is one hundred thirty dollars.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks who created and designed the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains that the manufacturer designs it and they introduced it to the US market.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks to confirm that they are just a distributor and did not create the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms that S3's statement is correct.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks what prevents him from going to the same manufacturer and selling a competing product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 admits that nothing stops S4 from doing that.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 deflects by mentioning their company brand and a successful Kickstarter campaign that raised twenty-five thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks if the Kickstarter money was just to get manufacturing done.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains they used Kickstarter to test the market and see if there was a proof of concept.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks if they have exclusive rights on the contract with the manufacturer.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 admits they do not have exclusive rights on the technology.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 expresses shock that they do not have exclusive rights.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 tells S4 to relax amidst the panel's reaction.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks what proprietary assets or advantages they actually have.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 explains they want the investment to create custom designs and innovate.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 states that their plan is a bad idea.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 exits, stating they lack self-awareness about being a sales organization rather than product creators.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks what their biggest obstacle is right now.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 struggles to answer and asks F1 for help.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 answers that the business is capital intensive and they need a Shark's connections.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 challenges them, stating they are not persuasive at all.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asserts that successful entrepreneurs always know exactly what their biggest obstacle is.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 repairs by stating their biggest obstacle is capital to fulfill inventory for opportunities.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 exits, arguing that passion, not money, solves problems, and she does not see enough passion.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks about their competition and whether Segway has a similar product.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 confirms Segway has a pair but notes they are more expensive due to brand recognition.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 remarks that brand recognition is everything in this market.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 exits, stating it is too hard to compete against an established brand name like Segway.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 points out that they do not own anything proprietary in a very competitive market.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 exits, bluntly stating that he hates the product and thinks it sucks.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks what their future vision and game plan is for the company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains their vision is to build a catalog of electric rideables with Chinese manufacturers.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 jokingly pretends to be S2 and exits on his behalf.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 exits, stating he simply does not trust them to be good custodians of his money.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 challenges them by advising them not to outsource sales but to go out and sell it themselves.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 tells S1 to let the founders leave and steep in their misery.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 wishes the founders good luck as they leave the tank.

decisions.note: They don't know what business they are in; they should focus on their sales expertise rather than product innovation.
They lack the passion needed to solve problems and grow, which cannot be fixed with money.
It is too hard to compete against established brand names like Segway given all their other issues.
He hates the product and thinks it sucks.
He does not trust them to be good custodians of his money to grow the business.
